newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bond yields edge up, wages still a worry.
newsitem.headline: Australian bond yields edge up, wages still a worry.

text.p: *Australian bond yields ended modestly higher on continued wage growth concerns, wiping out the rally which followed Tuesday's no rate change decision by the Federal Reserve.
Australian bond yields closed modestly higher on continued wage growth concerns, wiping out a rally which followed Tuesday's no rate change decision by the Federal Reserve.

Long-dated yields had dropped to their lowest level since February in after hours trading on the Fed news, but the move was reversed as hopes of a local easing were foiled by data showing a rise in wages growth through enterprise bargaining.
"Today's data will again disappoint the optimists looking for a further rate cut," said Craig James, senior economist at Colonial State Bank.
Private sector average annualised wage agreements through enterprise bargianing rose to 4.8 percent in the first quarter, according to data from the Department of Industrial Relations.

"If the wage rises secured at present under bargaining agreements are indicative of bargaining power in a modest labour market, then the risk further down the track as the labour market strengthens is likely to the upside," said Su-Lin Ong, fixed income economist at Hambros Bank Australia.
Further wages data is due on Thursday with the release of final wages data for the first quarter which will include the private and public sector split.
"Tomorrow's detailed data on average weekly earnings for the March quarter will need to be exceptional to reinvigorate rate cut speculation," Colonial's James said.
"That is, modest growth in the vicinity of 0.5 percent or less for the private sector growth of AWOTE in the March quarter," he added.
Preliminary AWOTE released earlier this month had shown overall growth at 1.3 percent in the first quarter for 4.6 percent annually and above the Reserve Bank's 4.5 percent "line in the sand".

The local market underperformed against the dollar bloc on today's wages report. The largest move on the day was against Canada, which rallied strongly in reaction to the unchanged Fed policy statement and was seen relieving recent pressure on the Canadian dollar.
